Photorealistic.description: Extremely lifelike rendering, indistinguishable from a high-quality photograph.

Oil Painting.description: Rich, textured brushstrokes and blended pigments in the style of classical oil paint.

Watercolor.description: Soft, translucent washes of color with visible paper texture and gentle bleeding.

Digital Art.description: Clean, polished illustration created with digital painting tools.

Pixel Art.description: Retro-style artwork composed of visible square pixels, common in classic video games.

Vector Art.description: Crisp, scalable shapes with flat colors and clean outlines.

Anime.description: Japanese animation style with expressive eyes, clean lines, and stylized shading.

Manga.description: Black-and-white Japanese comic style with screentone shading and dynamic linework.

Comic Book.description: Bold outlines, halftone dots, and vivid colors in the style of Western comics.

Sketch.description: Loose pencil or ink linework with an unfinished, hand-drawn feel.

Line Art.description: Clean, minimal artwork built purely from outlines without shading.

Low Poly.description: Stylized 3D look built from a small number of flat polygonal facets.

Concept Art.description: Polished illustrative artwork used for film/game pre-production, often moody and cinematic.

Matte Painting.description: Photorealistic painted environment, traditionally used as a film backdrop.

Charcoal Drawing.description: Smudgy, high-contrast monochrome drawing with deep blacks and soft gradients.

Acrylic Painting.description: Bold, fast-drying paint with vibrant flat or layered color.

Ukiyo-e.description: Japanese woodblock print style with flat color areas and flowing contour lines.

Stained Glass.description: Colored sections separated by dark lead lines, like a cathedral window.

Impressionism.description: Loose visible brushwork capturing light and atmosphere over fine detail, like Monet.

Art Nouveau.description: Flowing organic lines, floral ornament, and elegant figures in the style of Mucha.

Blueprint.description: White technical linework on blue paper, like an engineering schematic.

Claymation.description: Stop-motion clay look with fingerprints, handmade bumps, and soft shapes.

Graffiti.description: Bold spray-paint street art with drips, tags, and layered colors.

Retro Game.description: Artwork styled like a classic 8/16-bit era video game — chunky pixels, game-chrome feel, and HUD-era digital rendering.

Cel Shaded.description: Flat color areas bounded by bold ink outlines, like hand-painted animation cels.

Ghibli.description: Studio Ghibli / Hayao Miyazaki style — lush hand-painted backgrounds, gentle rounded character design, and warm naturalistic light.

90s Anime.description: Late-80s/90s OVA-era anime — angular faces, spiky hair, dramatic action poses, and thick confident ink lines.

Frutiger Aero.description: Mid-2000s tech optimism aesthetic — glossy aqua glass, bubbly shapes, water droplets, sky-blue gradients, fresh grass and fisheye lens flare, like Windows Vista / iPod-era UI.

Early 3D (N64).description: Mid-90s console 3D: stable low-poly geometry, Gouraud shading, tiny textures smeared soft, and distance fog hiding the draw depth.

Early 3D (PS1).description: Mid-90s console 3D: chunky low-poly geometry with affine texture warping on angled surfaces, slight vertex jitter, nearest-neighbor textures, and heavy ordered dithering.

Vintage Storybook Illustration.description: Golden-age printed book/comic plate look: engraved pen-and-ink linework, flat limited spot colors, halftone print grain, and theatrical ornamental composition.

8-bit (NES).description: NES-era pixel art: chunky 8×8 tiles, bold black outlines, 2-3 colors per sprite from a harsh fixed palette, on a 256×240 frame.

16-bit (SNES).description: Rich 16-bit era game art: lush hand-drawn pixel scenes, smooth color gradients, parallax layers, and Mode 7-style rotated planes.

Cartoon Saloon Style.description: Flat graphic 2D feature-animation look: filled shapes with confident ink contours, geometric dot-eyed characters, poster-like drapery folds, and watercolor-textured backgrounds.

Painterly.description: Rendered with visible painterly brushstrokes and blended color, keeping the texture of hand-painted artwork.

VGA Game.description: DOS-era PC game screenshot: dithered 256-color painted scenes and simple pixel sprites, like a late-80s/early-90s point-and-click adventure.

Soviet Auteur Animation.description: Poetic mid-century Soviet animation: hand-inked cel characters over painterly gouache backgrounds, muted naturalist palette, soft diffused light, and dreamlike pacing — like Norstein's Hedgehog in the Fog.

Disney Animation (Renaissance).description: Lush hand-painted watercolor backgrounds with expressive cel characters, musical-theater drama and warm saturated color — like 90s Disney features.

Golden Age Animation.description: Vintage 1930s-40s animation: rubber-hose characters with pie-cut eyes, bouncy squash-and-stretch motion, watercolor backdrops, and film-grain softness — early Disney and Fleischer.

2.5D.description: Pixel or sprite art placed in a 3D-style scene with layered depth planes and diorama staging — HD-2D, Paper-Mario, or New-Super-Mario-Bros-style depth.

Pop Art.description: Bold flat colors, halftone dots, and comic-derived mass-media imagery in the style of Warhol and Lichtenstein.

Risograph.description: Risograph print look: grainy fluorescent inks, slight color misregistration, and visible paper texture.

Retro CG Render.description: Glossy late-90s CGI character render: smooth airbrushed shading, bold rim light, and a saturated toy-plastic sheen — N64-era game box art like Banjo-Kazooie or Donkey Kong Country's pre-rendered look.

Matte.description: A non-reflective surface that diffuses light evenly.

Metallic.description: A shiny and reflective surface that mimics metal properties.

Glossy.description: A smooth, polished surface with sharp, bright reflections.

Glass.description: Transparent or translucent material with refraction and specular highlights.

Bark-like.description: A rough, textured surface resembling tree bark.

Wooden.description: Warm organic texture with visible grain and knots.

Marble.description: Smooth stone with elegant veining patterns.

Rusty.description: Oxidized, corroded metal with orange-brown patina and flaking texture.

Velvet.description: Soft, plush fabric with a dense light-absorbing pile.

Iridescent.description: Surface that shifts color depending on viewing angle, like a soap bubble.

Holographic.description: Rainbow-shifting reflective surface with futuristic shimmer.

Brushed Metal.description: Metal with fine parallel scratches giving a dull satin sheen.

Ceramic.description: Glazed pottery surface — smooth, hard, and slightly glossy.

Paper Mache.description: Rough, layered paper texture with a handmade feel.

Isometric.description: A 3D-like perspective where all axes are equally foreshortened at 120-degree angles; common in strategy games and pixel art.

Dimetric.description: A perspective similar to isometric but with two axes foreshortened unequally.

Bird's Eye View.description: A top-down perspective looking directly down onto a scene.

Worm's Eye View.description: Viewed from ground level looking up, making subjects appear towering.

Wide Angle.description: Expansive field of view with slight distortion, capturing more of the scene.

Macro.description: Extreme close-up revealing tiny details invisible to the naked eye.

Fisheye.description: Ultra-wide lens look with strong curved distortion at the edges.

Dutch Angle.description: Tilted horizon line creating tension and dynamism.

Over-the-Shoulder.description: Framed from behind a subject's shoulder, common in film and games.

Low Angle.description: Camera positioned below the subject looking up, making it appear heroic, imposing, or monumental.

High Angle.description: Camera positioned above the subject looking down, making subjects feel small, vulnerable, or surveyed.

First-Person POV.description: Seen directly through the character's own eyes, with hands or a weapon often visible at the frame edges, like an FPS view.

One-Point Perspective.description: All depth lines converging on a single central vanishing point — corridors, roads, and tunnels drawn head-on.

Three-Quarter View.description: Subject turned about 45 degrees from the camera, showing face and body at their most dimensional — the classic character-sheet angle.

Front View.description: Subject facing the camera square-on, symmetrical and direct, like a character-selection pose.

Profile View.description: Subject shown in strict side view, like a coin portrait or walk-cycle reference.

Symmetrical.description: Perfectly mirrored composition around a central axis.

Silhouette.description: Subject rendered as a solid dark shape against a brighter background.

Leading Lines.description: Composition guides the eye along converging lines toward the subject.

Negative Space.description: Large areas of emptiness deliberately framing a small subject.

Panoramic.description: Very wide framing capturing a sweeping horizontal expanse.

Minimalist Composition.description: Extremely sparse framing with few elements and lots of space.

Maximalist Composition.description: Densely packed frame overflowing with detail and objects.

Golden Hour.description: Warm, soft sunlight shortly after sunrise or before sunset.

Neon Lighting.description: Glowing colored light, often pink/cyan, with a cyberpunk feel.

Chiaroscuro.description: Strong contrast between light and dark for dramatic depth, like Caravaggio.

Backlit.description: Subject lit from behind, creating a glowing rim and silhouetted front.

Soft Diffused.description: Even, gentle light with no harsh shadows, like an overcast day.

Volumetric.description: Visible rays of light through fog or dust (god rays).

Bioluminescent.description: Organic glowing light emitted by the subject itself.

Studio Lighting.description: Controlled, professional three-point lighting with clean shadows.

Candlelit.description: Warm, flickering light with deep surrounding shadows.

Blue Hour.description: Deep blue ambient light just before sunrise or after sunset.

Dappled Light.description: Patches of light broken up by foliage or objects, creating spotted shadow patterns.

Dreamy.description: Soft, hazy, and ethereal with a gentle idealized feel.

Eerie.description: Unsettling and mysterious, on the edge of unsettling.

Melancholic.description: Quietly sad and reflective, often with muted tones.

Utopian.description: Idealized, perfect world — clean, bright, harmonious.

Nostalgic.description: Warm memory-evoking feel, often with vintage color grading.

Surreal.description: Illogical, dreamlike juxtapositions in the style of Dalí or Magritte.

Epic.description: Monumental, awe-inspiring scale that dwarfs the viewer.

Cozy.description: Warm, intimate, and inviting — soft textures and a sense of home.

Pastel.description: Soft, pale, desaturated colors with a gentle feel.

Vaporwave.description: Neon pinks, purples, and cyans with retro 80s/90s nostalgia.

Earthy Tones.description: Warm browns, greens, and ochres inspired by nature.

Duotone.description: Image rendered in only two contrasting colors.

Neon Palette.description: Saturated electric colors against dark backgrounds.

Sepia.description: Warm brown-tinted tones like an aged photograph.

Complementary.description: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel (e.g. teal & orange) for strong contrast.

Analogous.description: Neighboring hues on the color wheel for harmonious blending.

Limited Palette.description: Constrained to a small fixed set of colors (8–32), like classic game sprites — flat color bands instead of smooth blends.

Jewel Tones.description: Deep, richly saturated hues — emerald, oxblood, sapphire, and antique gold.

Muted Palette.description: Desaturated, grey-undertoned colors with a subdued, quiet mood — washed-out rather than pale.

Cyberpunk.description: High-tech dystopia with neon, rain, and sprawling megacities.

Steampunk.description: Victorian-era technology powered by steam, brass, and gears.

Retro Futurism.description: The future as imagined in the 1950s-70s — chrome, fins, atomic motifs.

Medieval.description: Castles, knights, and rustic villages of the Middle Ages.

Art Deco.description: 1920s glamour with geometric patterns, gold, and symmetry.

Solarpunk.description: Optimistic green future with lush vegetation and sustainable tech.

Dieselpunk.description: Gritty interwar-era tech aesthetic with heavy machinery.

Baroque.description: Ornate 17th-century opulence with dramatic movement and gold detail.

Ancient.description: Classical Greco-Roman world of marble temples, ruins, and mythology.

Prehistoric.description: Primordial world of caves, volcanoes, and colossal ancient life.

Feudal Japan.description: Edo-era setting with torii gates, castles, and samurai aesthetics.

Wild West.description: Dusty frontier towns, saloons, and endless desert landscapes.

Victorian Gothic.description: Dark 19th-century world of gothic spires, fog, and gaslight — no steam, just gloom.

Underwater.description: Submerged world with coral, caustic light, drifting particles, and distorted sound.

Dark Fantasy.description: Grim medieval fantasy of monsters, ruins, and shadowed forests — brooding and dangerous.

Celtic.description: Ancient-to-medieval Celtic world — knotwork, La Tène spirals, illuminated manuscript ornament, standing stones, and round towers.

Post-Soviet.description: Post-Soviet urban landscape — concrete panel-block housing, trolleybus wires, worn courtyards, and brutalist remnants.

Gritty.description: Rough, dirty, realistic texture with grime and wear.

Weathered.description: Aged by exposure — faded, cracked, and worn.

Glitchy.description: Digital corruption artifacts — color fringing, scanlines, datamosh.

Bokeh.description: Soft blurred background points of light from shallow depth of field.

Vignette.description: Darkened edges drawing focus to the center.

Film Grain.description: Analog camera noise giving a textured, cinematic feel.

Motion Blur.description: Streaking along the direction of movement to imply speed.

Lens Flare.description: Bright light scattering rings and streaks across the frame.

Double Exposure.description: Two images blended into one, like overlapping film photos.

Dithering.description: Gradients built from visible dot patterns (ordered/Bayer dithering) instead of smooth blends — classic limited-palette pixel art shading.

CRT.description: Faint CRT scanlines and phosphor glow over the whole image, like playing on an old tube TV.

Aqua Glass.description: Translucent blue-tinted glass with rounded highlights, refraction, and a wet polished sheen — 2000s aqua UI button look.

Bilinear Blur.description: Whole frame softened as if tiny textures were bilinear-filtered — the misty blur of a 320×240 console render.

Low-Res Textures.description: Chunky, visibly low-resolution textures stretched over geometry, with obvious tiling — scarce texture memory of a 90s console.

Crosshatching.description: Form and shadow built from dense layers of fine parallel pen lines, like an engraved book illustration.

Pixelated.description: Image broken into visible chunky pixels, like a low-resolution capture enlarged.

Glow.description: Bright light sources bleeding soft halos into their surroundings, like overexposed bloom.

Depth Fog.description: Background receding into thick atmospheric mist, layers dissolving with distance while the foreground stays sharp.

Depth of Field.description: Subject sharp while the background melts into soft focus blur, like a wide-aperture camera lens.

Forest.description: Dense woodland backdrop with thick trunks and layered foliage.

City Skyline.description: Urban backdrop of towers, rooftops, and glowing windows.

Cosmic.description: Deep space backdrop with stars, nebulae, and distant galaxies.

Ocean.description: Open sea backdrop with waves stretching to the horizon.

Mountains.description: Towering peaks and ridges receding into atmospheric haze.

Desert.description: Endless sand dunes under a vast empty sky.

Clouds.description: Subject floating among soft billowing clouds.

Garden.description: Lush flowerbeds, hedges, and winding paths.

Industrial.description: Factories, pipes, concrete, and heavy machinery.

Starry Night.description: Dark backdrop scattered with bright stars and galactic band.

White.description: Plain white studio background — clean product-shot isolation.

Black.description: Solid black background for dramatic subject isolation.

Gradient.description: Smooth color-fade background, from soft pastels to deep vignettes.

Transparent.description: Subject isolated with no background at all, like a cut-out asset (PNG-style).
